items.title: Rebuild Missing Files: add a "Last checked" timestamp alongside the existing "Last dealt with"
items.why: Director wants to know when a collection was last SCANNED, even if nothing was found missing -- "Last dealt with" only updates on a real fix, so a collection that's always clean never shows any recency info at all today.
items.prompt:
Director's ask: add a second, separate timestamp alongside the existing "Last dealt with" (queue: rebuild-missing-last-fixed, shipped) -- "Last checked", recorded every time a scan completes for a collection, REGARDLESS of whether anything was found missing. "Last dealt with" only updates on a real fix (Extract/Download Archive); "Last checked" answers a different question -- "when did I last confirm this collection was clean (or at least looked at it)", even on a scan that found zero problems.

REUSE, DON'T REINVENT: extend the exact same lightweight store already built for this -- `lib/rebuild-missing-last-fixed-state.js` (gitignored JSON file, collectionModId -> ISO timestamp map, same simple load/save pattern as `lib/backup-ratio-dismiss-state.js`). Add a sibling `lastChecked` map next to the existing `lastFixed` one in the same file/same JSON structure (not a second file) -- `markChecked(collectionModId)` / `getLastChecked(collectionModId)`, mirroring `markFixed`/`getLastFixed` exactly. Same collectionModId-keying rationale already documented in that file's own header (resets are correct behavior when a collection's staging folder changes identity, not a bug).

SCOPE:
1. `lib/rebuild-missing-last-fixed-state.js`: add `markChecked`/`getLastChecked` alongside the existing pair, extending `DEFAULT_STATE`/`loadState`/`saveState` to cover both maps.
2. `web/rebuild-missing-routes.js`: call `markChecked(collectionModId)` once per collection at scan completion -- unconditionally, unlike `markFixed` which only fires on a real fix. Find the real per-collection completion point in `lib/missing-files-scan.js`'s `scanCollections` (~line 211-254, the per-collectionModId loop) and call this from the route handler that already owns `lastFixedState` (matching the existing layering -- the lib itself doesn't import the state store, the route does), not from inside the lib.
3. Also include `lastChecked` in the same `GET /collections` response that already returns `lastFixed` (`item.lastFixed = lastFixedState.getLastFixed(item.modId)`, ~line 88) -- add the equivalent `item.lastChecked = lastFixedState.getLastChecked(item.modId)` right alongside it.
4. `web/public/rebuild-missing-app.js`: display both on the picker card's sub-line, matching the existing `— Last dealt with: {date}` convention (~line 165-166). Two real timestamps on one card needs a sensible display decision -- if both exist and are close/identical (a fix always implies a check happened), don't show redundant near-duplicate text; if only one exists (checked but nothing to fix, or vice versa -- though a fix without ever completing a scan shouldn't be possible given the scan-then-fix flow), show just that one. Use your own judgment on the exact layout (same line vs. a second line) and flag it in the handoff rather than guessing silently, since this is a real small UX call.

VERIFY LIVE: run a real scan against a collection that comes back completely clean (zero missing files) -- confirm `lastChecked` updates even though `lastFixed` doesn't. Run a real scan + a real fix on a different collection -- confirm both timestamps update appropriately. Reload the page and confirm both persist (not just an in-memory optimistic update). Handoff with what you tested and your own display-layout call.
